# The verification layer on a real map

The map is one Dynamic World tile (southern Peru, 2019-06-09) as olmoearth-inferencex 1.20.3 ships it: Dynamic World's class probabilities averaged over 40 m windows (4 x 4 of its 10 m pixels), with the expert's class for each window, the majority class of its annotated pixels where at least half of it was annotated. The population is the 15,813 of the tile's 16,384 windows that the expert annotated and whose probabilities are finite, one window each (one pixel of the GeoTIFF this script wrote, placed on the tile's recorded centre in its UTM zone, approximately, not on the source raster's own grid). The error rate checked is that of each window's arg-max class over them, not Dynamic World's 10 m accuracy, and the certificate is of that GeoTIFF.

No Studio key and no LLM: this script called the agent's verification tools through its default tool registry, in the order the agent calls them, and recorded each call as the lead agent does. The tile went in as a direct run read by olmoearth_scores_from_file with windows of one pixel, since a certificate's sample is drawn from the map's own raster. Every tool called is in the agent's default registry. Paths are written relative to the run's work folder, `<work>`. Map and expert labels: Dynamic World test tiles, Zenodo record 4766508, CC BY 4.0 (Brown et al., Scientific Data, 2022). olmoearth-inferencex averaged the probabilities over windows and stores them as float16 (its sample/NOTICE.txt).

## What each tool returned

Each row is one call, in the order made, with its key arguments and its key result; every figure is the tool's, as it returned it (rates as the tools write them). The estimates, the zone and the certificate read the labels from each plan's own sheet (`labels_path`), which this script filled for the windows the plan drew, as a labeller would: the expert's class in `reference_class`, and `wrong` 1 where it differs from the sheet's `map_class`.

|---|---|---|---|

No zone was certified, so no certificate was written and neither certificate check ran.

## Does each interval cover the true error rate of the tile's 40 m windows

This check is the script's, not the agent's. It is computed from the expert label of every window of the population, which a real user does not have; the tools saw only the labels of the windows each plan drew.

| Check | Tools' figure | Truth (expert label of every window) | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| The population's error rate | - | 3,048 of 15,813 windows wrong: 19.3% | - |
| Interval valid at every sample size, random design (call 4) | 14.8% to 23.9% | 19.3% | covers |
| Interval this design earns, random design (call 4) | 14.8% to 23.9% | 19.3% | covers |
| Interval valid at every sample size, class design (call 8) | 11.8% to 25.2% | 19.3% | covers |
| Interval this design earns, class design (call 8) | 11.4% to 30.7% | 19.3% | covers |
| Review set at budget 0.05 (call 2): its share of the map's errors | 791 windows | 532 of the 3,048 errors (17.5%); the attainable ceiling, min(1, budget / error rate): 26.0% | - |
| Certified zone (call 5) | no zone certified | - | - |

One run is one draw: an interval that covers the truth here, or misses it, is not evidence about how often such an interval covers it (its coverage rate). The same holds for the zone: its statement may fail on up to delta of all draws (olmoearth-inferencex's `ISSUED_NOTE`), so one zone at or under alpha here does not show that the guarantee holds, and one over it does not show that it fails.

The line below it is the interval estimate prints without --valid, unchanged: under the confidence and proportional designs Wilson's on the design's effective sample size, which is nominal (in the research record it covered 91.3% at 100 labels on a 200-window map, exp105; 92.7% near a census, 300 of 306 labelled; and at least 93% on the other graded cells, exp78); under `--design condition`, `class` and `profile` the union bound over the strata, which holds too; under a random sample the same exact interval. They do not hold jointly, and a share the map draws outside its own interval is flagged on that interval alone. The line below each is the table estimate prints without --valid, unchanged.

### Error rate (`olmoearth_estimate_map_error`)

- Map: scores file `<work>/scores_run_dynamic-world_cbd2b294_p1.json`.
- Error rate: 17.4%, estimated from 360 labels on a population of 15,813 windows.
- Interval valid at every sample size (95%): 11.8% to 25.2% (method: stratified by map class; valid at every sample size: the betting interval for a stratified sample drawn without replacement (the interval grade gives; the technical report's Theorem 1), the strata labelled in full added exactly).

- Labels, design and seed: 360 labels on the class design, seed 0; design file `<work>/design_scores_971becd8_class_360_s0.json`.
- Per class: Ranked by user's accuracy (of the windows the map puts in a class, the share the labels agree with) over the 8 classes with at least 5 map-labelled windows, the lowest are class 0 (0 of 10 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval valid at every sample size 0.0% to 0.0%, 95% interval this design earns 0.0% to 0.0%), class 8 (0 of 50 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval valid at every sample size 0.0% to 1.9%, 95% interval this design earns 0.0% to 1.9%), class 2 (0 of 50 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval valid at every sample size 0.0% to 4.7%, 95% interval this design earns 0.0% to 4.7%) and class 5 (0 of 50 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval valid at every sample size 0.0% to 6.6%, 95% interval this design earns 0.0% to 6.6%).
- olmoearth-inferencex's note on class 0: fewer than 30 labelled windows (10 the map calls this class, 0 the reference does); the exact intervals are wide
- olmoearth-inferencex's note on class 8: fewer than 30 labelled windows (50 the map calls this class, 0 the reference does); the exact intervals are wide
- olmoearth-inferencex's note on class 2: fewer than 30 labelled windows (50 the map calls this class, 0 the reference does); the exact intervals are wide

- Limit stated by the tool: Error rate 17.4%: valid 95% interval 11.8% to 25.2%, class design, 360 labels.
- olmoearth-inferencex's note: Each class's interval is its own 95% statement; the intervals do not hold jointly at 95%. The whole-map rate weights each class by its share of the map and can hide a class that is much worse. Each class's own interval is exact. The whole-map interval takes each class's exact interval at 1 - 0.05/L, where L is the number of classes not labelled in full, and weights it by the class's share of the map, so it covers at least 95% by construction; it is wider than the usual stratified interval. What the design buys is each class's own accuracy: every class gets at least its floor of labels, or all its windows, and the rest go in proportion to class size (Olofsson et al. 2014). If only the whole-map rate is needed, --design random can give a narrower interval.
- olmoearth-inferencex's note: --valid: the first interval covers the whole-map rate at least 95% of the time for every map and every number of labels, with no normal approximation: strata labelled in full enter exactly, one stratum labelled in part takes its exact hypergeometric interval, and two or more take the betting interval for a stratified sample drawn without replacement, the method grade uses. The valid interval was 1.6 to 1.7 times as wide as the confidence design's Wilson interval and 0.6 times the class design's union bound on the demo tile (aicr job 1554014).
- olmoearth-inferencex's note: --valid: each interval on a line marked valid holds at 95% on its own, for every map and every number of labels: the user's accuracy over the windows the map calls the class in each stratum (exact where they lie in one stratum labelled in part), the producer's accuracy from two such intervals at 97.5% each (a box), and the share over the strata.
